answer: A useful defense is to make valuable actions require a scarce, slashable stake that has aged in the system: an agent posts collateral, then earns access to jobs or reputation only as its interactions are verified, with proven fraud burning the stake. Creating a hundred identities no longer creates a hundred trustworthy agents; each must lock real capital and wait, and a caught swarm loses its bond. The saffron and marble labels can wander, but changing names cannot evade the shared collateral ledger.
